newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says 6 firms study Las Bambas copper deposit.
newsitem.headline: Peru says 6 firms study Las Bambas copper deposit.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Thursday six firms had signed agreements with state miner Minero Peru to evaluate the Las Bambas copper deposit prior to its privatization in the second quarter next year.
"Six companies interested in the project have signed drilling agreements with Minero Peru to study the area," the government's privatization chief, Jorge Gonzales Izquierdo, told Congress.
Minero Peru plans to auction the Las Bambas deposit provided the firm can clear up a legal problem involving a third party making claims on the property.

Las Bambas only has proven reserves of 17 million tonnes and probable reserves of 27 million tonnes, but it has a rich content of copper, between 1.8 percent and 2.2 percent, according to Minero Peru.
Minero Peru President Jorge Kawamura said recently that between 700 and 800 million tonnes of reserves would need to be found to make Las Bambas viable to mine.

The Las Bambas sale is part of Minero Peru's ongoing privatization of its deposits. The company plans to relaunch its sales with the auction of the Bayovar phosphate deposit next February and hopes to complete the privatization program by mid-1998.
